successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Buganda of the nineteenth century: the gazetteer's Buganda region with Buddu (Masaka, Lwengo, Bukomansimbi and Kalungu districts), without the Mubende, Nakasongola and Kiboga land held by Bunyoro and…

ledger.x: c. 1300: Kato Kintu founds Buganda in Busiro. 'unification around the 13th century by the first king, Kato Kintu'; infobox 'Founded by Kato Kintu: 12th/13th/14th century'; 'Likely founded between the 12th and 14th centuries, with the first state covering Kyadondo, Busiro, and Mawokota'. The year 1300 is a placeholder…
Late 18th century: Buganda captures Buddu from Bunyoro.
17th-18th centuries (1800 is a placeholder): Buganda grows from the first state of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota to the whole Buganda region.
Late 18th century: Kooki becomes a tributary of Buganda.
1891: Mwanga places Buganda under the company.
31 March 1893: 'the IBEAC formally ended its involvement in Uganda'; British protection follows on 18 June 1894.
June 1894: the tributary relation ends with the kingdom.
18 June 1894: Uganda becomes a British protectorate.

wars.name: Battle of Rwangabi
wars.outcome: Bunyoro victory: its army 'achieved a significant victory against the Baganda' in February 1886 in the armed struggle over the ivory trade; no border moved.

wars.name: Buganda religious wars and the Lugard intervention
wars.outcome: Mwanga II was ousted in a Muslim coup in 1888; Lugard came for the Imperial British East Africa Company in 1890; Mwanga signed a treaty in 1891; in 1892 'the Protestants and Catholics resumed their struggle for supremacy'.

certainty.note: Kingdom frontiers are approximate throughout: counties named by the page, no survey or treaty line before the colonial period.
